title: Forge provider wait v1 (an additive payload extension at event_schema 1)
description: Decision 0103 rulings 2(a), 3 and 4(a): the optional, absent-by-default payload fields that record a provider's rate-limit cool-down and the probe that ends it. `effect/failed.waits` (and, from decision 0103 slice 4c2, `effect/indeterminate.waits`) is one entry per refused site: the journal tag (absent for an inline seat), the provider and route the driver already resolved, the provider's bounded words, its retry-after when given, the computed `until`, the round of that site's waits within the effect's episode, and the length the engine computed under that entry's own route's bounds. `effect/failed.refused` is the typed refusal that ended the run in a park, written beside the `run/parked` that follows so a crash between the two appends cannot lose it: the cause, the invocation-site tag where one applies, the provider, the route where resolved, the provider's words, its retry-after when given, and the computed length and declared maximum where the engine reached them. A `waits` entry exists only where an `until` exists; `refused` exists even where none can. `effect/started.probes` is the answers the dedicated one-turn probes gave before their retry, one entry per answering probe with the site, provider, route and when it answered; a single seat writes one entry. The fields are optional and absent by default, are published as a numbered extension at event_schema 1 under the amended rule in contracts/README.md, and are never read by `fold`: the engine reads them from the effect's own events and `RunState` gains nothing. A present entry that cannot be read refuses by name, never as absent.

waits.description: Present on a terminal `effect/failed`, and (slice 4c2) on `effect/indeterminate`, only when at least one site's typed rate-limit refusal recorded a wait. One entry per refused site; a single seat carries exactly one.

refused.description: Present on an `effect/failed` that parks on a typed rate-limit refusal, beside the `run/parked` that follows (decision 0103 slice 4c1, this fix round). It keeps the refusal's facts even where no `until` can be written.

probes.description: Present on the retry's `effect/started` only after a dedicated probe answered, so the wait's end has a record: one entry per answering probe, and a single seat writes one. A probe that ended without an answer writes none.

site.description: The invocation-site tag the journal already uses for checkpoints and provenance: '<member>' for a panel member, '<step>' for a sequence step, '<step>:<member>' for a member inside a step panel. Absent for an inline seat, which has no tag.

provider.description: The provider name the adapter's declaration uses (claude, lanetally, codex, dsh, exec, ...), filled from the adapter and never parsed from prose.

route.description: The route the driver serves the pinned model on: the concrete model id's prefix before its first `/` (decision 0036 ruling 2), from the one predicate the producer and this pattern share. A route that could not be resolved parks naming it and records no wait: a null route would be a provider-wide hold over unrelated routes.

words.description: The provider's bounded evidence line, in its own words. One line, clamped, never a transcript.

retry_after_seconds.description: The provider's own retry-after in whole seconds, when it gave one. It is the wait as given and is never lengthened; a later round doubles only the route's declared default. When present it must equal `seconds`; the reader enforces that equality, which draft-07 cannot compare across two properties.

seconds.description: The length of this round's wait in whole seconds, as the engine computed it under THIS entry's route's bounds: the provider's retry-after when it gave one, else that route's default doubled for the round. An episode sums the recorded lengths and never recomputes an earlier wait under a later route's bounds.

until.description: The computed end of this round's wait: now plus `seconds`. A resume reads it and waits the remainder; the maximum is judged from `seconds` and the episode, never from the remainder.

rounds.description: Which round of this site's waits within the effect's episode this is: one for the first refusal at this site, two for the next. The episode's seconds are summed across its sites; this wait's `seconds` is the length computed under this entry's own route's bounds at that round (decision 0103 ruling 3).

site.description: The invocation-site tag of the refusal, tagged as `waits.site` is: '<member>' for a panel member, '<step>' for a sequence step, '<step>:<member>' for a member inside a step panel. Absent for an inline seat.

cause.description: Why the typed rate-limit refusal ended the run in a park. Closed: an unknown cause refuses where it is read. `no-end` is a wait whose computed length the journal cannot spell as an RFC 3339 `until`, so no wait can be taken; `past-maximum` is a computed wait past the declared maximum.

provider.description: The provider name, filled from the adapter as `waits.provider` is.

route.description: The route the driver resolved, absent only for `route-unresolved`: a provider-wide hold would hold unrelated routes.

words.description: The provider's bounded evidence line, in its own words, as `waits.words` carries it.

retry_after_seconds.description: The provider's own retry-after in whole seconds, when it gave one.

seconds.description: The wait's computed length in whole seconds, present only for a cause that computed one (`past-maximum`, `no-end`).

max_seconds.description: The declared maximum the computed length was judged against, present with `seconds`.

site.description: The invocation-site tag the probe asked, tagged as `waits.site` is. Absent for an inline seat.

provider.description: The provider the probe asked, as the wait entry names it.

route.description: The cooled route the probe asked, as the wait entry names it.

answered_at.description: When the probe's first model-output answer arrived. A session start, `accepted`, a spawn, a hang, a deadline or an error is not an answer and records none.
